title: Deduction Priority and Combined Caps — Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders
content:
Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders are taken from a benefit payment in a fixed rank order, and each kind is held within a combined cap measured against the net payable after the overpayment offset. The table lists the six kinds in rank order, 1 first.

| Priority rank | Kind | Combined cap (share of net payable after overpayment offset) | Sharing of the cap among several orders of the kind | Taken in part when the remaining net is short | Minimum remaining net for any deduction | Skipped payment reported to the payee agency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order | 50% (0.50) | In proportion to the orders' weekly amounts | Yes | $0.00 — any amount | Yes |
| 2 | Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order | 50% (0.50) | In proportion to the orders' weekly amounts | Yes | $0.00 — any amount | Yes |
| 3 | Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding | 100% (1.00) | Not applicable | Yes | $0.00 — any amount | No |
| 4 | Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding | 100% (1.00) | Not applicable | Yes | $0.00 — any amount | No |
| 5 | SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation | 50% (0.50) | Not applicable | No | $25.00 | Yes |
| 6 | SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error | 25% (0.25) | Not applicable | No | $25.00 | Yes |

**Footnotes to the table**

(a) *Priority rank* is the order in which deductions are taken from one payment; rank 1 is taken first.

(b) *Combined cap* is a ceiling on all deductions of that kind together, expressed as a share of the payment's net payable after the overpayment offset. A cap of 100% means the kind may take up to the whole of that net.

(c) *Sharing of the cap* states how the combined cap of a kind is divided when the claimant has several orders of that same kind. The two child support kinds share by weekly amount; the other four kinds show "not applicable".

(d) *Taken in part* states whether a deduction is taken partially when the remaining net is below the computed amount. "No" for both SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds means that, when the remaining net is below the computed amount, those deductions are not taken in part.

(e) *Minimum remaining net* is the smallest remaining net from which a deduction of that kind is taken at all. $0.00 means any amount; for both SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds it is $25.00.

(f) *Skipped payment reported* states whether a payment from which the kind's deduction could not be taken is reported to the payee agency: yes for both child support kinds and both SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds, no for the two voluntary income tax kinds.

**Illustration of the cap column (hypothetical figure)**

For a hypothetical benefit payment whose net payable after the overpayment offset is $400.00, the combined caps read from the table are: $200.00 for each child support kind, $400.00 for each voluntary income tax kind, $200.00 for SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation, and $100.00 for SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error. Each figure is that kind's cap share multiplied by the $400.00 net.
